title: Sushi Rice (Hoshihikari, Rice Cooker)
description: A separately prepared 300 g dry-rice batch for approximately four sushi rolls, seasoned with rice vinegar, sugar and salt without kombu.
steps: Immediately discard the first rinse of cool water, then gently swirl and rinse the grains 3–4 times until the water is less cloudy. Avoid aggressive scrubbing.
Drain in a sieve for 10 minutes. Add the washed rice and measured 340 ml water to the rice cooker. Soak in that same water for 30 minutes before starting.
Cook with a white-rice or sushi-rice setting. Once complete, rest with the lid closed for about 10 minutes if the cooker does not already include a steaming rest.
While the rice cooks, warm the unseasoned rice vinegar, sugar and salt just enough to dissolve the crystals; do not boil or reduce.
Transfer hot rice to a broad nonreactive bowl. Distribute the seasoning evenly while cutting and folding gently, not stirring or mashing. Fan intermittently until glossy and around body temperature.
Keep covered with a clean, slightly damp cloth while assembling sushi. Use promptly; do not leave cooked rice at room temperature for extended periods.
notes: Hoshihikari japonica: start with 340 ml water for 300 g dry rice in a rice cooker; adjust future batches by 10–15 ml based on your specific cooker and rice age.
This makes roughly 650–700 g prepared sushi rice, sufficient for approximately four medium rolls or a mixed assortment of nigiri, gunkan and hand rolls.
No kombu is used, and no replacement seasoning is needed.
The rice-vinegar seasoning assumes unseasoned vinegar, not bottled pre-sweetened sushi vinegar.

Sushi rice without verified acidification should not be held unrefrigerated for more than 2 hours; if the room is above 32°C, limit to 1 hour. Refrigerate leftovers promptly, although cold rice loses its ideal texture.
